name: VL53L0X ToF Distance Sensor
accuracy: 4% std dev at 120 cm white 88% indoor 33 ms budget
output_type: distance mm
strengths: Cheapest ST FlightSense part; tiny; STEMMA QT; 25 deg cone is the widest single-zone cone in the Adafruit ST line
weaknesses: 2 m headline is the long-range API profile and the datasheet restricts it to dark conditions only; grey-17% drops to 80 cm indoor and 50 cm outdoor overcast; superseded by VL53L4CD at the same price
source_url: ST DocID029104 Rev 1 Table 11 and section 5.1

name: VL53L1X ToF Distance Sensor
accuracy: +/-20 mm in dark; +/-25 mm under ambient
output_type: distance mm
strengths: Programmable region of interest can be swept across the 16x16 SPAD array for a coarse pseudo-multizone image; short mode is almost ambient-immune at 130 cm
weaknesses: ST publishes only a DIAGONAL 27 deg for this part, and its diagonal is a separately measured number rather than the geometric diagonal of the detection volume, so the 19.3 deg horizontal used here is DERIVED as 2*atan(tan(13.5)/sqrt(2)) and is an inference, not a published figure. It is the best available basis for sizing a ring and it may be optimistic. The published 27 deg is a DIAGONAL FoV; horizontal is 19.3 deg so a 360 deg ring needs about 19 units. Long mode collapses from 360 cm to 73 cm under 200 kcps/SPAD ambient

name: VL53L4CD ToF Distance Sensor
accuracy: +/-7 mm below 100 mm; +/-3% beyond 200 mm white 88% indoor
output_type: distance mm
strengths: 100 Hz ranging - the fastest single-zone part in the lane - and a -30 to +85 C range; the right cliff and low-ring part
weaknesses: 1300 mm is a 50%-detection white-88% figure; against a grey-17% target at 90% detection it is a 450 mm sensor

name: VL53L4CX ToF Distance Sensor
accuracy: +/-8 mm below 110 mm; +/-3% to +/-5% beyond 110 mm indoor
output_type: distance mm; multiple target distances per cone
strengths: Best dark-target reach of any single-zone part here - 2100 mm on a 17% grey chart at 90% detection indoors - and histogram multi-object output reports a chair back and the wall behind it in one cone
weaknesses: Driver needs about 50 kB of flash so it will not fit an ATmega328; 6 m is a 50%-detection white-88% number

name: VL53L3CX Multi-Target ToF
accuracy: +/-7 to +/-10 mm over 25-90 mm; +/-2.5% to +/-5% beyond 110 mm indoor
output_type: distance mm; up to four simultaneous target ranges
strengths: Reports up to four ranges inside one cone so a thin object that leaves the background visible can be told from a broad one that occludes it - a weak but free occupancy-depth cue
weaknesses: Pololu markets it as 500 cm; the ST datasheet has no 5 m row at all - 310 cm white and 170 cm grey-17% are the real typicals. Histogram driver is not recommended for 8-bit MCUs

name: VL6180X ToF Proximity and Ambient Light Sensor
accuracy: noise max 2.0 mm; offset error max 13 mm
output_type: distance mm plus calibrated lux
strengths: Ten times lower current than the VL53 family at 1.7 mA and the only part in the lane with a calibrated ambient-light output; excellent cliff and stair-edge sensor; 850 nm so it does not interfere with 940 nm VL53 parts
weaknesses: 100 mm of guaranteed range is inside the bumper line of a 350 mm robot - useless as a perimeter sensor. Pololu carrier 2489 is marked End-of-Life Rationing

name: VL53L4ED Low-Power ToF
output_type: distance mm
strengths: ST low-power variant of the L4CD aimed at battery consumer products; 800 mm is claimed under 5 klx with special settings
weaknesses: No Adafruit or Pololu breakout exists; every figure is ST product-page only because st.com would not serve the datasheet PDF in any research pass

name: VL53L5CX 8x8 Multizone ToF
accuracy: +/-5% at 8x8 dark; +/-11% at 8x8 grey-17% under 5 klux
output_type: distance mm per zone plus per-zone motion indicator
stock_status: in stock at Pololu; SparkFun SEN-18642 on backorder
strengths: Cheapest 64-zone depth grid; pin and driver compatible with the VL53L7CX; free per-zone firmware motion indicator is a real animate-versus-inanimate primitive at single-digit mW in autonomous mode
weaknesses: Dark/sunlit corner zones collapse to 650 mm typical and 400 mm minimum; I2C only so no fast SPI firmware boot; Arduino library untouched since 2023; ST footnotes its own 17% grey chart as measuring 13% in IR at 940 nm

name: VL53L7CX Wide-FoV 8x8 Multizone ToF
accuracy: per-zone; ST publishes the same accuracy structure as the L5CX
output_type: distance mm per zone plus per-zone motion indicator
strengths: Widest ST grid FoV at a true 60 deg horizontal so a 360 deg ring closes with 10 units instead of 12; pin-to-pin and driver compatible with the VL53L5CX
weaknesses: Wide FoV is bought with range one for one - at 8x8 under 5 klux against a 17% target it is a 250-350 mm sensor and even 4x4 gives only 500-550 mm. A ring you cannot use in a lit room

name: VL53L8CX 8x8 Multizone ToF
accuracy: +/-11 mm at 20-200 mm; +/-5% beyond 200 mm at 8x8; corner zones degrade up to 4%
interface: I2C 1 MHz addr 0x29 or SPI 20 MHz
output_type: distance mm per zone plus per-zone motion indicator
strengths: Best ambient-light performance of the CX family - 1650 mm inner and 1550 mm corner against a 17% grey target under 5 klux at 4x4/30 Hz; 20 MHz SPI collapses the 84 kB firmware boot; actively maintained Arduino library; autonomous 8x8 at 1 Hz costs 6.7 mW
weaknesses: The 400 cm headline is a dark-room white-target inner-zone 4x4 figure; 8x8 tops out at 15 Hz; every unit boots at 0x29 with a volatile address so a ring needs a mux or per-sensor XSHUT GPIOs

name: VL53L8CH Histogram Multizone ToF
accuracy: identical to the VL53L8CX; histogram bin equivalent range 37.5 mm
output_type: distance mm per zone plus raw per-zone return histogram
stock_status: active; no hobby breakout priced in any lane
strengths: The only part in the study that carries material and shape information rather than range alone - a flat box face puts its return in 1-2 bins of 37.5 mm while a curved furry body spreads over about 7 bins with a long fur tail; pin-to-pin with the VL53L8CX
weaknesses: A 64-zone 18-bin CNH frame is 6108 bytes and 56 ms of bus time at 1 MHz I2C so two sensors saturate a bus at 15 Hz; SPI is only 3 MHz against the CX 20 MHz; price not published in any source lane

name: VL53L7CH Wide-FoV Histogram Multizone ToF
output_type: distance mm per zone plus raw per-zone return histogram
strengths: CNH histogram output on the 60 deg wide-FoV optics
weaknesses: Inherits the VL53L7CX range collapse under ambient light - 250-350 mm at 8x8 against a 17% target in 5 klux - on top of the CNH bus cost
source_url: ST DS13865 Rev 6 range tables; CH firmware per DS14310 Rev 3

name: VL53L9CX 2268-Zone dToF Camera
accuracy: up to 1% of distance
output_type: depth plus 2D IR plus reflectance plus confidence
stock_status: 0 in stock at DigiKey; 1 unit due 2026-10-28; 4 week factory lead
strengths: A generational jump - each zone subtends about 1 deg against 5.6 deg for an 8x8 VL53L8CX so a cat at 10 ft is 4.5 x 8 zones instead of 0.8 x 1.6; BSI stacked dToF claimed independent of target colour
weaknesses: MIPI CSI-2 / I3C only so it needs a Linux-class SoC camera port per sensor; no Arduino CircuitPython or ESP-IDF driver exists; the 8.8 m headline carries NO published per-reflectance or per-ambient table; both eval boards are at zero stock
source_url: ST VL53L9CX product page and press release p4783; DigiKey 29294599

name: TMF8801 ToF Distance Sensor
accuracy: +/-5% beyond 200 mm; +/-10 mm from 100-200 mm
output_type: distance mm
strengths: The one part in the lane whose datasheet publishes a full range-versus-reflectivity-versus-ambient matrix; cheapest dToF at 9.95; 24 deg FWHM long-range cone
weaknesses: Host must push a several-kilobyte firmware patch on every boot; 18% grey under a 100 klux sunlight equivalent falls to 550 mm; datasheet warns any target reported beyond 2500 mm is no object
source_url: ams-OSRAM DS000648 v10-00 Figure 19 and section 7.8

name: TMF8806 ToF Distance Sensor
accuracy: +/-3% beyond 500 mm in 5 m mode; +/-2% beyond 2000 mm in 10 m mode
output_type: distance mm
strengths: Longest-reaching single-zone dToF here against a dark target - 3250 mm on an 18% grey card in 350 lux indoor light; 30 deg long-range cone covers floor to knee at conversational range; no firmware patch needed for 5 m mode
weaknesses: The 10 m rows of the datasheet are WHITE WALL figures and must not be read as obstacle range; one layer of tape on the cover glass costs 340 mm of range on an 18% grey target; Adafruit and the datasheet disagree on FoV and Adafruit admits no results past 5 m

name: TMF8820 3x3 Multizone dToF
accuracy: +/-5 mm from 20-200 mm in short-range mode
output_type: distance mm per zone
stock_status: not sold by Adafruit; SparkFun Qwiic dToF Imager uses this family
strengths: 3x3 zones hold their range far better than the 8x8 mode - 5000 mm centre and 4000 mm corner on an 18% grey card in 350 lux LED light
weaknesses: Nine zones is a coarse obstacle map not a silhouette; Adafruit showed a TMF882x breakout prototype in 2024 but no product page exists as of 2026-09-12 so price is unread

name: TMF8821 4x4 Multizone dToF
accuracy: +/-5 mm from 20-200 mm in short-range mode
output_type: distance mm per zone
stock_status: not sold by Adafruit; sold as the SparkFun Qwiic dToF Imager
strengths: Selectable zone maps 3x3 4x4 and 3x6 and five selectable FoVs; dynamic cover-glass calibration is built in
weaknesses: Edge and corner zones lose more than half the centre range - 1400 mm corner on an 18% grey card even in 350 lux LED light

name: TMF8828 8x8 Multizone dToF
accuracy: +/-10 mm from 10-20 mm; +/-5 mm from 20-200 mm in short-range mode
output_type: distance mm per zone
stock_status: not sold by Adafruit as of 2026-09-12
strengths: 64 zones over a 41 x 52 deg field - the widest vertical field of any grid part in the study
weaknesses: The 8x8 table is taken at 125 k iterations against 550 k for the 3x3 and 4x4 tables so it is not comparable; corner zones collapse to 200-500 mm on an 18% grey card. 64-zone mode is a near-field mode not a room-scanning mode

name: RPLIDAR A1M8 360 Laser Range Scanner
accuracy: 1% of range below 3 m; 2% from 3-5 m
supply_v: 5 scanner plus a separate 5-10 V motor rail
output_type: range mm plus heading plus quality per sample
strengths: One device one cable gives a full 360 deg planar map; Class I eye-safe and the datasheet states safety to human and pet; mature SDK plus ROS 1 and ROS 2 drivers publishing sensor_msgs/LaserScan
weaknesses: Triangulation not dToF; range is conditioned only on the words White objects and NO dark-target figure is published anywhere; datasheet claims indoor and outdoor without sunlight; 170 g and about 2 W continuous with a spinning bearing and no published MTBF; 0.15 m blind radius
source_url: Slamtec LD108 A1M8 datasheet rev 2.1 and v2.2 Figure 2-1

name: RPLIDAR C1 360 dTOF Scanner
accuracy: +/-30 mm; 15 mm resolution
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
strengths: dTOF so it publishes an honest low-reflectance figure of 6 m at 10% reflectance; 40000 lux ambient immunity; 0.05 m blind radius suits a 350 mm chassis; IP54; 110 g; 500 points per revolution is enough to scan-match and hence to know a cluster is new
weaknesses: Still one plane so everything above and below it is invisible at every range; 230 mA figure is a reseller listing not confirmed against the Slamtec datasheet; -10 to 40 C only

name: RPLIDAR A2M12
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
stock_status: no USD price published; Slamtec directs to sales
strengths: 16 kHz sampling gives 0.225 deg angular resolution - four times the A1M8
weaknesses: 0.2 m minimum range leaves no usable margin on a 350 mm chassis whose skin is at 0.175 m; the 12 m figure carries no reflectivity condition on the Slamtec A2 page; price not verified

name: RPLIDAR S2
interface: serial on S2; Ethernet on S2E
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
strengths: 32 kHz sampling at 0.1125 deg; 80 klux ambient immunity; IP65; optical scanning area only 18 mm tall which is exactly what a small shell needs
weaknesses: Price not published anywhere in the research; far above the C1 and LD19 class in cost and size for a 350 mm indoor robot

name: RPLIDAR S2L
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
strengths: Cheapest member of the S2 family; same 0.1125 deg resolution and 0.05 m blind radius
weaknesses: Price not published; ambient-light rating not separately stated for the S2L

name: RPLIDAR S2P
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
strengths: Longest reach in the S2 family at 50 m against 90% and 15 m against a 10% target
weaknesses: Range far beyond anything a 350 mm indoor robot can use; price not published

name: LDROBOT LD06 360 Scanner
accuracy: +/-30 mm typical and +/-45 mm max; 15 mm resolution
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
stock_status: superseded - inno-maker LD06 URL now serves an LD19P
strengths: 42 g and 0.9 W - by far the best mass and power per 360 deg of coverage; 30 kLux ambient immunity; 38.6 mm square footprint suits a small chassis; 12 m is conditioned on a 70% target which is rare honesty
weaknesses: 10000 h rated lifetime is about 14 months of continuous running; no LD06 price was confirmable anywhere; buy the LD19 instead
source_url: LDROBOT LD06 datasheet hosted by Inno-Maker

name: LDROBOT LD19 / LD19P 360 dTOF Scanner
accuracy: 10 mm from 300 mm to 12000 mm
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
stock_status: in stock at Inno-Maker as LD19P
strengths: 10 mm ranging accuracy across the whole span - better than the LD06 and the C1; 0.9 W; 30 kLux; FDA Class 1; the practical replacement for the LD06
weaknesses: Waveshare quotes 0.02-12 m with NO reflectivity condition at all - assume it is the same 70% class figure as the LD06 until LDROBOT says otherwise; -10 to 40 C

name: Waveshare D500 LiDAR Kit
accuracy: 10 mm from 300-500 mm; 20 mm from 500-2000 mm; 30 mm from 2-12 m
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
stock_status: price not read in any research pass
strengths: 0.72 deg angular resolution in the same 38.6 mm square LD-class footprint
weaknesses: 1.45 W - 60% more than the LD19 for the same range; no anti-glare figure stated on the Waveshare wiki page; no reflectivity condition on the 12 m

name: YDLIDAR X2
accuracy: 2 cm systematic error at range below 1 m; 3.5% relative from 1-6 m
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
stock_status: no USD price published on ydlidar.com
strengths: 8 m at 80% reflectivity indoors for a 126 g unit; 0.72 deg at the default 6 Hz
weaknesses: Its own datasheet lists a lighting environment of 0 to 2000 lux - this is not a sunlight sensor; triangulation; 1000 mA start current

name: YDLIDAR X4 PRO
accuracy: 2 cm at distance below 1 m; 3.5% relative from 1-6 m
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
stock_status: no USD price published on ydlidar.com
strengths: 0.43 deg angular resolution at 6 Hz for a triangulation unit at this price class
weaknesses: Published service life is 1500 hours - about 62 days of continuous running - which makes it a consumable not a component on an always-on robot

name: YDLIDAR G4
accuracy: 2 cm at range below 1 m; 2.0% relative from 1-8 m
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
stock_status: no USD price published on ydlidar.com
strengths: 0.2 deg angular resolution at 5 Hz and 9000 Hz ranging - the densest triangulation unit here
weaknesses: Triangulation so it inherits the ambient-light weakness of the family; 1000 mA start current; 0.12 m blind radius; price not verified

name: YDLIDAR T-mini Plus
accuracy: 20 mm over 0.05-12 m
output_type: range mm plus heading per sample
stock_status: no USD price published on ydlidar.com
strengths: True ToF not triangulation; 60 kLux ambient immunity - the highest in this table; publishes a 10% reflectivity figure of 4 m; 38.6 mm square LD-class footprint; 0.05 m blind radius
weaknesses: 4 m against a 10% target is only two thirds of the RPLIDAR C1; 6 Hz default scan rate; price not verified

name: Livox Mid-360 3D LiDAR
accuracy: <=2 cm at 10 m; <=3 cm at 0.2 m; angular precision <0.15 deg
output_type: 3D point cloud
stock_status: price not published on the spec page
strengths: The only unit here that breaks the single-plane limitation - a -7 to +52 deg vertical field over a full 360 deg azimuth; 40 m at 10% reflectivity; Class 1
weaknesses: 265 g and 6.5 W average rising to 14 W in self-heating mode and it needs an Ethernet host; the vertical field looks UP not down so a unit at 1000 mm first reaches the floor about 8.1 m out and everything inside that radius is below the beam. fov_v is recorded as 0 per the 360-scanner convention

name: Benewake TFmini Infrared ToF
accuracy: +/-4 cm from 0.3-6 m; +/-6 cm from 6-12 m; 5 mm resolution
output_type: distance cm
strengths: Publishes the most explicit ambient-light and reflectivity breakdown in the lane - 0.3-3 m holds under 100 klux outdoor glare AND against a 10% black target; 100 Hz; under 120 mW
weaknesses: A 2.3 deg beam needs 157 units to tile 360 deg; the manual tabulates a minimum reliable target of 8 cm at 2 m so a cat tail or a chair leg edge-on can be missed; the manual warns high-reflectivity targets break it
source_url: Benewake manual SJ-PM-TFmini-T-01 A03 Tables 1 and 2

name: Benewake TF-Luna
accuracy: +/-6 cm from 0.2-3 m; 1 cm resolution
output_type: distance cm
stock_status: not sold by Adafruit; price not verified in this pass
strengths: 8 m for under 0.35 W and under 5 g - nothing in the ST ToF family competes on range per watt; 1-250 Hz frame rate
weaknesses: FoV wavelength laser class and ambient immunity are all NOT PUBLISHED on the Benewake pages read; a roughly 2 deg cone makes it a single guard beam not a perimeter sensor; no classification

name: Benewake TFmini-S
output_type: distance cm
stock_status: not sold by Adafruit; price not verified in this pass
strengths: 12 m in a 42 x 15 x 16 mm 5 g package
weaknesses: Accuracy resolution frame rate power FoV wavelength laser class and ambient immunity were all NOT PUBLISHED on the pages read; the page structured data also carries an inconsistent 11 g weight

name: Garmin LIDAR-Lite v3
accuracy: +/-2.5 cm typical below 5 m; +/-10 cm typical at 5 m and beyond; nonlinear below 1 m
output_type: distance cm
strengths: 40 m against a 70% reflective target with the condition actually printed in the row label; 270 Hz update
weaknesses: A 0.46 deg beam is a laser pointer - a 16 mm spot at 2 m threads straight past a cat leg and reports the wall; Adafruit repeats two wrong numbers for accuracy and update rate; 2-per-customer cap rules out a tiled ring
source_url: Garmin LIDAR-Lite v3 Operation Manual and Technical Specifications

name: Garmin LIDAR-Lite v4 LED
accuracy: +/-1 cm to 2 m; +/-2 cm to 4 m; +/-5 cm to 10 m
output_type: distance cm
strengths: 4.77 deg cone gives a usable 170 mm spot at 2 m; LED emitter not a laser; 2 mA idle
weaknesses: No Garmin-hosted specification document could be retrieved so EVERY number is reseller-page only and whether a target-reflectivity condition exists for the 10 m is unverified; 59.95 x 76 units for a ring is absurd; 2-per-customer cap

name: Sharp GP2Y0A21YK0F Analog IR Ranger
accuracy: output voltage differential 1.9 V typical between 10 and 80 cm
output_type: analog voltage; not a calibrated distance
strengths: Position-sensitive-detector triangulation so reflectance barely moves the output - Sharp Fig 2 plots 90% white and 18% grey nearly coincident across 10-80 cm. Reflectance-blindness is its one advantage over dToF
weaknesses: The response curve is NON-MONOTONIC below 10 cm so a wall at 1.6 cm reads the same as one at 25 cm - exactly the case a mobile robot must detect; beam width is NOT PUBLISHED by Sharp Adafruit or Pololu so perimeter coverage cannot be computed; Adafruit 3 V at 10 cm is unsupportable - use 2.3 V

name: Sharp GP2Y0A02YK0F Analog IR Ranger
accuracy: 0.4 V typical output at 150 cm
output_type: analog voltage; not a calibrated distance
strengths: Longest-reaching Sharp analog part at 150 cm and the same 90%-versus-18% reflectance insensitivity
weaknesses: Same non-monotonic near-field ambiguity below 20 cm and the same unpublished beam width; current and update rate are not on the Adafruit page; Adafruit own advice on that page is to use sonar above 1 metre
source_url: Sharp GP2Y0A02YK0F datasheet via Pololu mirror

name: Sharp GP2Y0D810Z0F Digital Distance Switch
accuracy: digital threshold only; no distance output
output_type: digital present/absent
strengths: 400 Hz sample rate and a 2.56 ms steady-state update for a bumper-imminent trigger
weaknesses: Returns a bit not a distance; 100 mm of reach; Adafruit itself recommends the ST VL6180X as the replacement

name: Sharp GP2Y0D805Z0F Digital Distance Switch
output_type: digital present/absent
strengths: 5 to 50 mm digital trip point for a last-millimetre bumper skirt
weaknesses: Unbuyable; 50 mm of reach; no distance output

name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Sonar Distance Sensor
accuracy: resolution not published
output_type: echo pulse width proportional to range
strengths: Colour-blind and the cheapest way to see clear glass which defeats every optical sensor in the study; best working band is 10-250 cm
weaknesses: Clones have no chained-trigger support so N units must be sequenced in firmware; a smooth surface more than about 15 deg off perpendicular bounces the ping away and reads clear; fur wool and thick coats absorb 40 kHz; no classification whatsoever

name: RCWL-1601 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor 3V/5V
accuracy: 1 mm resolution
output_type: echo pulse width proportional to range
strengths: Runs from 3 V as well as 5 V at only 2.2 mA and is pin-compatible with the HC-SR04; 1 mm resolution; sees glass
weaknesses: Beam is quoted only as plus or minus 15 to 20 deg; mutual interference between co-located 40 kHz units is severe; soft targets absorb; best band is 10-250 cm not the headline 450 cm

name: US-100 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor 3V/5V
output_type: echo pulse width or serial range
strengths: UART mode removes the timing-critical echo measurement from the host; onboard temperature compensation; 2 mA
weaknesses: Narrow sub-15 deg cone means many units for a perimeter; same specular and soft-target failures as the rest of the class; no classification

name: MaxBotix LV-MaxSonar-EZ0
accuracy: 1 inch resolution
interface: analog Vcc/512 per inch; PWM 147 us/in; serial 9600
output_type: distance in inches
strengths: The only part in the whole study whose datasheet publishes a people-detection claim - can detect people up to approximately 10 feet - and MaxBotix defines the 1-inch dowel pattern as the reliable people zone; widest and most sensitive beam in the LV line; best for soft objects
weaknesses: Beam is published as four dowel-target detection zones not an angle so no cone can be computed; 49 ms per range cycle so an 8-sensor round robin is 2.5 Hz; nothing published for animals; anything closer than 6 inches reports as 6 inches

name: MaxBotix LV-MaxSonar-EZ4
accuracy: 1 inch resolution
output_type: distance in inches
strengths: Narrowest beam in the LV-EZ line and the least sensitive to side objects - good for a corridor or a single forward guard beam
weaknesses: The narrow beam is exactly wrong for perimeter coverage; same 20 Hz cycle and soft-target absorption as the EZ0

name: Large Ultrasonic Sensor with Horn UART
accuracy: 1 mm resolution
output_type: distance mm
strengths: 7.5 m with the horn fitted - the longest ultrasonic reach in the Adafruit catalogue; 75 deg without the horn is the widest acoustic cone available
weaknesses: 28 cm dead zone is larger than a 350 mm robot can tolerate at the skin; unbuyable; 50 mA peak

name: VCNL4200 Long Distance IR Proximity and Light Sensor
accuracy: 16-bit proximity count; not a calibrated distance
output_type: reflected-IR count plus lux
strengths: Longest-reaching optical proximity part Adafruit lists at a datasheet 1.5 m; also gives 0.003 to 1570 lux
weaknesses: Adafruit itself tempers the claim to a practical 50-100 cm and the datasheet publishes NO target reflectivity or size behind the 1.5 m; drives the IRED at up to 800 mA; reports a count not a distance

name: VCNL4030 Proximity and Lux Sensor
accuracy: proximity count; not a calibrated distance
output_type: reflected-IR count plus lux
strengths: 300 mm proximity plus a 0.004 to 16768 lux ambient channel in one STEMMA QT part
weaknesses: 300 mm is inside the bumper line of a 350 mm robot; returns a count not a distance; I2C address not stated on the product page

name: VCNL4040 Proximity and Lux Sensor
accuracy: proximity count; not a calibrated distance
output_type: reflected-IR count plus lux
strengths: The right part for cliff detection pointed down from the chassis skirt - it closes the near-field hole that every dToF ranger leaves inside its own minimum range, for under 6 dollars
weaknesses: 200 mm and a count not a distance; must never be treated as an obstacle sensor

name: APDS9960 Proximity Light RGB and Gesture Sensor
accuracy: 8-bit proximity count; not a calibrated distance
output_type: 8-bit proximity count plus RGB plus gesture
strengths: Adds RGB colour and a four-direction gesture channel that no other part here has
weaknesses: Adafruit states only up to a few centimetres and publishes NO numeric proximity range and NO gesture range so max_range_m is deliberately left empty; the I2C address is not on the product page; centimetres not metres

name: STEMMA Reflective Photo Interrupter TCRT1000
accuracy: digital or analog reflectance; not a distance
output_type: reflectance high/low
strengths: Millimetre-scale cliff and edge detection for under 5 dollars with no bus at all
weaknesses: Range is quoted only as millimetres with no number so max_range_m is left empty; a dark floor reads as a false cliff which is the documented failure mode of every reflective IR cliff sensor

name: AMG8833 Grid-EYE IR Thermal Camera Breakout
accuracy: +/-2.5 C typical; 0.25 C output resolution; NETD 0.16 C at 10 Hz
output_type: degC per pixel
strengths: The cheapest imaging thermal part and the only modality that separates alive from not-alive AND sees a MOTIONLESS target - a sleeping cat is invisible to MTI radar and to PIR and visible here; 10 Hz is fast enough for a 1.7-4 Hz gait cue; 4.5 mA
weaknesses: Cannot see a room-temperature object at all so it answers requirement (a) not at all; only two I2C addresses exist so a ring needs a mux; apparent temperature is mostly a range measurement in disguise below full pixel fill; optical axis gap is plus or minus 5.6 deg which is three quarters of a pixel of boresight error per unit; 15 s to stabilise

name: AMG8833 IR Thermal Camera FeatherWing
accuracy: +/-2.5 C typical; 0.25 C output resolution
output_type: degC per pixel
strengths: Same Grid-EYE silicon in Feather form factor with a display-ready carrier
weaknesses: Identical 8x8 limitations as PID 3538 and the Feather stack format is awkward on a distributed perimeter ring

name: MLX90640 32x24 IR Thermal Camera Breakout 55 Degree
accuracy: +/-1 to +/-2 C frame accuracy; NETD 0.1 K RMS at 1 Hz best pixel
output_type: degC per pixel
strengths: 768 pixels at 30.0 mm/m horizontal so a clothed torso fills a pixel out to 15 m and a cat out to 7.8 m - no sub-pixel dilution anywhere in the useful range; classifies a human past 7 m and a pet to about 3 m; tilted 20 deg down it is the best single thermal configuration in the catalogue
weaknesses: Melexis publishes NO detection range - the 7.0 m here is the lane-computed pixel-subtense limit not a vendor figure; the programmed refresh rate applies per SUBPAGE so a full frame arrives at half rate and a fast target tears across the two halves; up to 4 min of thermal stabilisation; one frame is about 42 ms of 400 kHz bus time so a multi-sensor ring is bandwidth-bound to roughly 1.4 Hz each
source_url: Melexis MLX90640 datasheet Rev 12 3 Dec 2019 Tables 14 15

name: MLX90640 32x24 IR Thermal Camera Breakout 110 Degree
accuracy: +/-1 to +/-2 C frame accuracy; NETD 0.1 K RMS at 1 Hz best pixel
output_type: degC per pixel
strengths: Best cost per degree of any thermal array here - a 360 deg thermal ring closes with six units instead of nine; 3.1 x 3.4 px on a cat at 3 ft
weaknesses: FoV is bought with range exactly one for one - pet classification reaches about 1.5 m against 3 m for the 55 deg part and a bare face starts diluting beyond 3.3 m; out of stock so it must be sourced from Melexis Waveshare or a distributor; Melexis publishes no detection range
source_url: Melexis MLX90640 datasheet Rev 12 3 Dec 2019 Table 15

name: STHS34PF80 IR Presence and Motion Sensor
accuracy: 0.0125 C RMS equivalent temperature noise at AVG_TMOS 32; ambient accuracy +/-0.3 C
output_type: object temperature LSB plus presence and motion flags
strengths: Genuinely better than a PIR - it holds a STATIONARY human, needs no Fresnel lens so it fits behind a small aperture, draws 10 uA, and ships embedded presence and motion algorithms; the right always-on parked-robot wake-up layer at 14.95
weaknesses: It has exactly ONE sensing element so it reports something warm is somewhere in an 80 deg cone - no bearing no size no shape and no contribution at all to human-versus-pet; 4 m is specified against a 70 x 25 cm object without a lens
source_url: ST DS13916 Rev 2 July 2023 Table 3 and section 1

name: MLX90614 Contact-less IR Thermometer 3V
accuracy: +/-0.5 C typical; object range -70 to +380 C
output_type: object and ambient temperature in C
strengths: Wide -70 to +380 C object range and a simple two-register I2C read
weaknesses: NO detection range is published so max_range_m is left empty; the datasheet states accuracy is valid only if the object fills the FoV and the measured value is the average of all objects in the field - across a 90 deg cone that is the room not the person; Adafruit redirects buyers to the AMG8833

name: MLX90614 Contact-less IR Thermometer 5V
accuracy: +/-0.5 C typical; object range -70 to +380 C
output_type: object and ambient temperature in C
strengths: 5 V variant of the same xAA 90 deg optical family
weaknesses: Same unpublished detection range and same fills-the-FoV caveat as PID 1747; Adafruit redirects buyers to the STHS34PF80

name: UTi165H Thermal Camera Imager
accuracy: +/-0.5 C at 1 m; sensitivity under 50 mK; 6 mrad IFOV
output_type: thermal image on a handheld display
strengths: 19200 pixels at 8-14 um - by far the highest thermal resolution in the catalogue
weaknesses: A battery handheld with no machine-readable output; the 30-45 C measurement window is tuned for fever screening and clips everything at room temperature; NO detection range is published - only a 1 m optimal measuring distance - so max_range_m is left empty; not embeddable

name: UTi165K Thermal Camera Imager with USB Video
interface: USB-C real-time video out plus LCD
output_type: thermal video over USB
strengths: USB-C video output makes the 160x120 frame machine-readable in principle
weaknesses: The 30-45 C window still clips room temperature so it cannot serve as a scene thermal array; 499.95 for one field of view; no detection range published

name: PIR Motion Sensor
output_type: digital motion bit
strengths: Longest-reaching PIR in the catalogue at about 7 m and a 120 deg cone for under 10 dollars
weaknesses: Motion only - it cannot hold a static human at all; LEAST sensitive to radial motion so a person walking straight at the robot is the worst case; does not see through glass; responds to warm airflow which a drivetrain provides; on a driving robot the whole scene moves and the output saturates

name: Breadboard-friendly Mini PIR Motion Sensor
output_type: digital motion bit
strengths: 3.95 and a 3-pin header - the cheapest way to add a near-zero-power wake-up gate
weaknesses: 2-5 m with a 100 deg cone and motion only; same radial-motion blindness glass opacity and ego-motion saturation as every PIR

name: Mini PIR Sensor with Time and Sensitivity Control BS612
output_type: digital motion bit
strengths: 1.95 with onboard hold-time and sensitivity trimmers; lens focused at 5 m
weaknesses: Motion only and no static hold; a pet-immune lens cannot be replicated at robot height because the trick needs a 2.2 m mount; useless on a moving platform

name: mmWave Radar 24GHz Human Presence Detection Sensor 9m
chip: not published; CLI fingerprint matches Leapmmw HS2xx3A (inferred)
accuracy: 15 cm range index step; no range output
output_type: presence boolean only
strengths: Works in the dark and through a plastic shell; first-party ESPHome component; claims a sleeping or sitting person at 9 m; -40 to +85 C
weaknesses: Outputs a BOOLEAN ONLY - no distance no bearing no speed - so it is an occupancy switch not a perception sensor; factory clear latency is 10 s; the vendor FAQ states outright that it detects movement of all objects and warns the sensor must be fixed firmly which a drivetrain violates; detection distance carries no RCS reflectivity or clutter condition

name: mmWave C4001 24GHz Presence Sensor 25m UART
chip: C4001 module; silicon not published; HW string JYSJ_5807_A01
accuracy: NOT PUBLISHED - the datasheet states the distance is not calibrated and is reference only
output_type: target count plus range m plus radial speed m/s plus energy
strengths: Publishes its ranges split by target state - 25 m motion and 16 m stationary human - and returns real numbers rather than a bit; signed speed gives an approach/recede bit; volume tiers to 12.90 at 10 plus
weaknesses: DFRobot own datasheet disclaims the distance output as uncalibrated; ONE target maximum; presence and ranging modes are mutually exclusive; nothing below 1.2 m which is exactly the collision zone; a 1 m transition zone means the detection volume has soft non-deterministic edges; 15 s default clear latency; current NOT PUBLISHED
source_url: DFRobot C4001 SEN0609 datasheet V1 sections 1.1 and Characteristics

name: Gravity mmWave C4001 24GHz Presence Sensor 12m I2C and UART
accuracy: NOT PUBLISHED - same uncalibrated-distance disclaimer as SEN0609
output_type: target count plus range m plus radial speed m/s plus energy
strengths: Twice the vertical coverage of the SEN0609 on the same C4001 family - an 80 deg vertical beam puts a 300 mm pet in the beam from 0.72 m when mounted at 900 mm; I2C as well as UART; 22 x 30 mm
weaknesses: Same one-target limit uncalibrated distance mutually exclusive modes and 1.2 m ranging floor as SEN0609; the library accepts a 30 cm minimum which contradicts the published 1.2 m and DFRobot does not explain it; current NOT PUBLISHED

name: Fermion C4002 mmWave Motion and Static Presence Module
accuracy: range-gate resolution selectable 20 cm or 80 cm; no accuracy figure published
interface: UART 57600 to 1 Mbps plus configurable OUT pin
output_type: target state plus distance m plus speed m/s plus direction plus energy 0-99 plus per-gate bitmap plus lux
strengths: Best information per dollar of any DFRobot radar - 26 gates of 20 cm out to 5.2 m with a per-gate threshold 0-99 that lets you blind the first gates so the robot own shell stops dominating the CFAR window; widest and symmetric 120 x 120 deg beam; approach/recede direction bit; integrated 0-50 lux sensor; 8.30 at 10 plus
weaknesses: startEnvCalibration learns a STATIC background and the wiki requires an empty room - a driving robot invalidates it every frame; the store title says 10 m the wiki says 11 m and the repo says 11 m static - three vendor numbers; DFRobot example default report period is 1 Hz; current NOT PUBLISHED; no species classification of any kind

name: C1001 60GHz mmWave Indoor Fall Detection Sensor
accuracy: breathing 10-25 breaths/min; heart rate 60-100 bpm; both only 0.4-1.5 m at the chest
interface: UART 115200 plus IO1 fall level plus IO2 presence level
output_type: x/y track plus posture plus fall state plus static residency plus breathing rate plus heart rate
classification_output: fall detected; posture; sleep state; breathing rate; heart rate
strengths: The only DFRobot radar that outputs target coordinates and the only one that reports any class at all - posture fall and vital signs; 61-61.5 GHz so it does not interfere with the 24 GHz parts; the only DFRobot range figure with a published measurement condition (2.7 m ceiling mount)
weaknesses: The whole fall algorithm is a point-cloud posture classifier referenced to a 2.7 m DOWNWARD ceiling mount - bolted to a moving 1 m robot the reference frame it depends on does not exist; the API exposes no point cloud; the wiki FAQ says it can only detect if an object is moving and cannot count multiple individuals; respiration bands overlap cats and dogs almost entirely so no species label is possible; explicitly not a certified medical device

name: mmWave 24GHz Human Presence Sensing Module 6m
chip: Hi-Link HLK-LD2410 (inferred from a matching specification fingerprint)
accuracy: 0.75 m distance resolution from a 250 MHz sweep
interface: UART 57600 default plus GPIO OUT 3.3 V
output_type: presence bit plus per-gate moving and stationary energy plus target distance
strengths: The only DFRobot radar that publishes its sweep bandwidth (250 MHz) and the gate resolution that follows from it; the per-gate moving and stationary energy vector is the most information-rich cheap output DFRobot sells; 7 x 35 mm is the smallest radar footprint in the catalogue
weaknesses: VERTICAL FoV IS NOT PUBLISHED - DFRobot gives only plus or minus 60 deg without saying which axis; 250 MHz gives a 600 mm range cell which is 1.7 robot-widths deep; moving-versus-stationary range split is not published; the DFRobot 57600 default conflicts with Hi-Link own 256000; users report the LD2410 detecting someone through two layers of sheetrock

name: mmWave 24GHz Microwave Radar Distance Sensor 20m
chip: 24 GHz K-band FMCW; silicon not published
accuracy: +/-0.1 m; 0.01 m reporting resolution
output_type: distance cm to the nearest reflector plus an optional 126-bin range-FFT spectrum
strengths: The ONLY DFRobot radar honestly aimed at obstacles rather than presence - it ranges any reflector including static ones - and the only one that exposes raw pre-detection data, a 126-line range-FFT magnitude vector you can run your own ego-motion-aware CFAR on; publishes accuracy and resolution; 78 x 23 deg keeps the floor out of the main lobe
weaknesses: 0.5 m blind zone and a 23 deg vertical beam mean a 300 mm pet does not enter the beam until 2.95 m when mounted at 900 mm; 65.90 is five times a C4001; over 100 mA; 0 to 70 C only; no velocity output; the up-to-5-obstacles claim is about what the spectrum supports after YOUR peak-finding not a reported target list

name: Gravity Digital 10.525GHz Microwave Motion Sensor
accuracy: no range output; sensitivity set by an onboard potentiometer
output_type: single digital motion bit
strengths: The only part here whose beamwidth is published as an explicit -3 dB half-power figure; 13 dBm EIRP and -86 dBm receive sensitivity; works on living and non-living materials
weaknesses: TECH FIELD IS FORCED - this is 10.525 GHz X-band not mmWave, and the enumeration has no X-band value; it outputs ONE BIT so no range no speed and no presence-while-still; 48.5 x 63 mm is the largest radar here and large for a 350 mm robot; on a moving base everything has relative motion so the output saturates to motion

name: 5.8GHz Microwave Radar Module
output_type: presence level plus serial
stock_status: DISCONTINUED - retired from the DFRobot catalogue
strengths: By far the lowest-power radar DFRobot ever listed at 22 mA with a 120 x 120 deg beam in a 20 x 18 mm board
weaknesses: UNBUYABLE - the page is retained for documentation only and the listed price is 0.00; TECH FIELD IS FORCED since 5.8 GHz is not mmWave; the 11 m figure carries no measurement condition

name: mmWave 80GHz Liquid Level Detection Sensor 40m
chip: 77-81 GHz FMCW with a 4 GHz sweep
accuracy: +/-5 mm; 1 mm reporting resolution; native range resolution is 37.5 mm from the 4 GHz sweep
output_type: surface range in mm
strengths: The highest-performing radar silicon DFRobot sells - the only module with a published sweep bandwidth and therefore the only one with real range resolution; 30 mA; -45 to +85 C; the plus or minus 3 deg lens version is genuinely interesting as a single forward is-the-floor-still-there beam
weaknesses: TECH FIELD IS FORCED - 77-81 GHz has no enumeration value; it is a LEVEL GAUGE designed for one flat perpendicular reflector so the 1 mm is interpolated sub-bin precision on a specular return that a human body does not give; blind zone baud rate output frame and IP rating are all NOT PUBLISHED; zero classification

name: MR60BHA2 60GHz Breathing and Heartbeat Module
accuracy: breathing accuracy 90% typical
output_type: has_target plus num_targets plus distance plus breath rate plus heart rate
stock_status: Seeed part; price not read in any research pass
strengths: Names its silicon, which no DFRobot radar does; monolithic 2T2R transceiver with an ARM Cortex-M3 and 1 MB flash in 25 x 31.5 mm; ESPHome component exists
weaknesses: Chest breathing and heart rate only work from 0.4 to 1.5 m which is the window in which a robot is already about to collide; NO human-presence range appears anywhere in the datasheet; the ICC table says 600 mA max but the Precautions section demands a 3.1-3.5 V supply at 1 A or more with 50 mV ripple; the datasheet warns a radome distorts the beam and a robot shell IS a radome; outputs no x/y

name: MR60FDA2 60GHz Fall Detection Module
accuracy: fall recognition accuracy 90% typical
output_type: fall flag plus presence
stock_status: Seeed part; price not read in any research pass
strengths: Publishes its range condition honestly - the detection range is closely related to target RCS and environmental factors and it is normal for it to fluctuate
weaknesses: 2 m maximum sensing radius and a mandatory 2.2-3.0 m TOP mount are structural not tunable; the datasheet is a Beta Version whose own section 1 names a different part (MR60FDC1) from the cover; needs a 1 A supply; a robot shell acts as a radome the datasheet warns against

name: Person Sensor
accuracy: box confidence 0-100 and ID confidence 0-100; about 200 ms latency
output_type: face bounding box plus confidence plus recognition ID 0-7 plus is-facing flag
stock_status: DISCONTINUED - retired at SparkFun and The Pi Hut; the vendor exited hardware
strengths: Privacy by design - no raw image egress, metadata only, non-updatable firmware; 150 mW; a genuine drop-in identity channel at face height
weaknesses: RANGE IS NOT PUBLISHED - the docs say the bounding-box size serves as a distance approximation so the vendor never characterised one, and max_range_m is left empty; a FACE detector is not a PERSON detector so a turned back a profile or a seated person is invisible; requires illumination and dim-light capability is explicitly uncharacterised; the category has no stable supply
source_url: Useful Sensors person_sensor_docs and SparkFun retirement page

name: Gravity Offline Edge AI Gesture and Face Detection Sensor
zones: 1 frame; up to 10 faces or upper bodies
accuracy: no accuracy figure published
output_type: face and upper-body bounding boxes plus gesture class
strengths: Runs entirely offline on the module and reports up to 10 faces or upper bodies to 3 m for 14.90 - an upper-body class is materially more useful on a robot than a face-only class
weaknesses: The 85 deg figure is a DIAGONAL so it overstates the horizontal cone used for ring arithmetic; the model is closed and cannot be retrained; no pet class; needs ambient light like any camera; no distance output
